note: change_pwd_page (Password Separate Form) has no config, no permissions, no Drush, no plugins. It provides a standalone change-password page (/user/change-password -> /user/{user}/change-password, route change_pwd_page.change_password_form, form id change_pwd_form), hides the password fields on user_form, and integrates with Password Policy by writing password_policy.settings:change_password_route = 'change_pwd_page.change_password_form' on install. Password Policy IS enabled on this site, so medium/hard cases are grounded in that single integration key: medium seeds a known value and reads it back; hard requires setting it to the module's separate-form route, verified live. All scripts touch only that one key and restore the module's own install value (change_pwd_page.change_password_form) as baseline.

evals.prompt: The change_pwd_page (Password Separate Form) module is enabled on a Drupal 11 site. What URL does a logged-in user visit to change their password on the dedicated page, and where does that URL send them?
evals.expected_output: /user/change-password (route change_pwd_page.change_password) redirects the current user to /user/{user}/change-password (route change_pwd_page.change_password_form), the standalone ChangePasswordForm.

evals.prompt: How does the change_pwd_page module change the normal Drupal user account edit form (user_form)?
evals.expected_output: Via hook_form_alter on user_form it hides the new-password widget ($form['account']['pass']['#access'] = FALSE) and re-labels the current_pass description, so password changing is moved to the separate page.

evals.prompt: How does change_pwd_page integrate with the Password Policy module, and specifically which configuration value does it set?
evals.expected_output: On install it sets password_policy.settings:change_password_route to 'change_pwd_page.change_password_form' so Password Policy enforcement follows the separate change-password form.

evals.prompt: This site runs the Password Policy module. Inspect the live configuration and state which route Password Policy is currently configured to use for password changes (the change_password_route).
On this site, inspect the Password Policy configuration and report the exact route name currently set as its change_password_route.
evals.expected_output: password_policy.settings:change_password_route is currently 'user.pass' (a deliberately changed value; normally change_pwd_page sets it to change_pwd_page.change_password_form).

evals.prompt: On this site the Password Policy change_password_route is currently pointing at core's user.pass. Reconfigure Password Policy so that it uses the separate change-password form provided by the change_pwd_page module. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Set password_policy.settings:change_password_route to 'change_pwd_page.change_password_form' (drush config:set password_policy.settings change_password_route change_pwd_page.change_password_form).

evals.prompt: Password Policy on this site is set to change_pwd_page.change_password, but that is the redirect route, not the actual form. Point Password Policy at the correct change_pwd_page route that renders the separate change-password FORM. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Set password_policy.settings:change_password_route to 'change_pwd_page.change_password_form' (the form route), not change_pwd_page.change_password (the redirect controller route).
